data_processing_steps.description: Start from 10% Census sample (5,693,850 individual observations); drop individuals for whom a spouse cannot be identified (3,626 obs), same-sex couples (10,242 obs), and divorced/widowed/separated individuals (815,349 obs) — an overall reduction of ~14.6%.
Restrict to marriageable-age sample: women aged 23-53, men aged 25-55; drop couples where either partner falls outside the relevant age range. Resulting sample: 1,850,766 observations.
Drop individuals (and their spouses) with missing education (0.15% of obs) and individuals not reporting religion (8.5% of obs).
Restrict Muslim sample to individuals born in the UK or who arrived before age 18 ('British'/UK-raised), excluding 54% of Muslim observations whose marriage may have occurred before UK arrival.
Final estimation sample: 1,423,555 individuals, of whom 38,938 (2.7%) are identified as Muslim.

Construct the 'marriage migration' proxy: a same-ethnicity marriage between an ethnic-minority British individual (UK-born or arrived before 18) and a spouse who migrated after age 18; White British excluded (marriage migration ~0.4% among them) and same-ethnicity restriction applied since ~93% of observed marriage migration among minorities is same-ethnicity.
Treat cohabiting couples as single in the baseline; exclude same-sex couples; restrict to heterosexual matches.

Aggregate ethnic categories into five groups for estimation: White British, Other White, Indian, Pakistani/Bangladeshi, and Other (Pakistani and Bangladeshi combined given similar population share, religious practice, and income).
Define the type space for the structural model: age (3 ten-year bands: young/middle/old), education (college degree indicator), ethnicity (5 categories), and religion (Muslim indicator).

Apply a small-cell correction to zero/sparse match-count cells before minimum-distance estimation: mu_tilde = (mu_hat + delta)/(N + C*delta) * N, where delta is a small positive constant and C is the number of match/single cells.

Estimate joint surplus parameters via Minimum Distance Estimation (three-step: initial weighting matrix, delta-method variance estimate, re-estimation with efficient weight matrix), equivalent to least-squares regression of 2*ln[mu_xy/sqrt(mu_x0 * mu_0y)] on surplus covariates phi_xy.

Recover gender-specific 'outside market value' terms B_(y->x) and B_(x->y) directly from observed cross-market match counts and inside-market singles/matches using equations (eq:miggain1)/(eq:miggain2).

Solve for the equilibrium matching distribution (used for model fit and counterfactuals) via the Iterative Proportional Fitting Procedure (IPFP), alternating updates of single-women and single-men masses until convergence.

Construct an alternative lower-bound marriage-migration measure from Understanding Society Wave 1: classify as marriage migration only when the migrant spouse's reported arrival year is strictly after the marriage year.

Code a continuous 0-1 'relocation score' for 195 self-authored Muslim marriage biographies using a keyword scheme (1 = fully flexible on location, 0 = fixed-location requirement, intermediate values for partial/conditional flexibility).

Estimate fertility rates by couple religious-type (f_MM=3.07, f_MN=2.78, f_NM=2.46, f_NN=2.36) and religious-transmission probabilities (p_MM=0.978, p_MN=0.976, p_NM=0.238, p_NN=0.001) from Understanding Society fertility histories and parent/child religious affiliation, used in the two-generation extension.
